I have been using grunt at work, but recently I saw some projects on git hub that talk about gulp and webpack, but does not talk about setting up the project with grunt. That made me wonder if people moved from grunt to gulp and are now moving from gulp to webpack. Is this the case?

Yep, the best mentor I have in Javascript has moved to Webpack, and we're now deploying it for enterprise production software. He can probably articulate "why" far better than my abilities. I learned everything from this guy, we've worked on KnockoutJS, Backbone, and Angular projects together. Webpack is the new thing, lord knows if it'll last more than a year or two though. The Javascript fatigue is very real.

Grunt will open a file, do an operation, save that work to a file -> then open that file, do another operation on it, save it again -> then...

Gulp will open a file, pipe it to an operation, pipe it to another operation... then save the file.

The more efficient file operating process, a cleaner looking config file (opinion), and being able to specify operations programmatically in Gulp instead of as a mostly static config object in Grunt was my reasoning for making the switch.

Personally I haven't delved into Webpack, but can't deny it's popularity and I should look into it soon, but currently I'm having much fun and success using npm scripts in my build process.
